newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE euroyen dips slightly on Utsumi comments.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE euroyen dips slightly on Utsumi comments.

text.p: The key March three-month euroyen futures contract dipped slightly on Tuesday afternoon after Japanese government bonds (JGBs) eased on comments from a former Ministry of Finance (MOF) official, but the downside held firm and further losses were not expected, traders said.

Makoto Utsumi, former vice minister for international affairs at MOF, told Reuters Financial Television that JGBs are trading at "bubble" levels and prices are likely to undergo a downward correction due to increased Japanese economic activity. JGBs were sold as a result, putting euroyen futures under downward pressure, a city bank trader said.
But JGB losses were limited due to expectations that today's 4-yr JGB auction will be successful, and this also helped keep euroyen futures from dipping further, he added.
Market activity was lethargic overall as operators wait for the auction results, due out at 0530 GMT, as well as Japan's June industrial production figures, to be released on Wednesday.
The key March euroyen futures contract stood at 99.10 at 0422 GMT, down 0.01 from Monday's close.
